title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured Digital Marketer apprentice. This course covers the fundamentals of SEO, including keyword research, on-page and off-page optimization, and technical SEO. learning_objectives: Explain how crawling, indexing, and ranking determine whether a page can appear in search results
Classify the search intent behind a query and match it to an appropriate page type
Build a prioritized keyword map from research data
Analyze competing sites to find realistic ranking opportunities
Optimize a page's title, headings, metadata, and body copy for a target query
Design a site structure and internal linking plan that distributes authority
Diagnose crawlability, speed, and mobile issues that suppress rankings
Publish and optimize SEO content in a content management system
Plan an ethical off-page and link acquisition strategy

prerequisites: dm101 Introduction to Digital Marketing, or equivalent familiarity with digital marketing channels
Comfortable editing page content and metadata in a website or CMS

objectives: Explain how crawling, indexing, and ranking determine whether a page can appear in search results

lessons.title: Competitive and Content Gap Analysis

Produce a content gap list from a competitor comparison

lessons.title: On-Page Optimization
objectives: Optimize a page's title, headings, metadata, and body copy for a target query
Apply structured data markup where a rich result is warranted

lessons.title: Site Architecture and Internal Linking

sequencing_rationale: At 80 hours this is the largest course in the pathway, so it is the one that can afford to teach SEO in its natural dependency order rather than as a tactics list. Mechanism first (lessons 02-03: nothing about optimization is meaningful until the learner knows what indexing and intent are), then research (04-05: you cannot optimize for a target you have not chosen), then implementation in increasing scope - page (06), site (07), infrastructure (08) - then publishing workflow (09), then off-page (10, deliberately last of the tactics because link acquisition without a worthwhile page is wasted effort), then measurement (11), then a capstone audit that exercises all of it. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS - the intake description is truncated mid-word (it ends at 'leverage SEO tools to impro') and supplied no objectives or lesson titles, so: (1) The cut sentence was read as improving organic visibility, and lesson 11 is scoped to measurement and iteration; no specific claim from the truncated text was reconstructed. (2) The named topics - keyword research, on-page, off-page, technical SEO, search intent, SEO tools - are treated as the required spine, and everything else here is connective tissue. (3) Tools are taught tool-agnostically with Google Search Console as the one assumed-available tool; paid suites (Ahrefs, Semrush, Screaming Frog) are referenced as categories, and the reviewer should confirm which the program actually licenses. (4) Local SEO, international/hreflang, and e-commerce product-feed SEO are OUT of scope at this hour budget - flag if they are expected. (5) Content production beyond SEO writing is dm270's job; lesson 09 covers only the publish-and-optimize step. (6) Paid search is dm230's; lesson 03 draws the boundary but does not cross it.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can diagnose and remediate technical SEO defects, including crawl directives, indexation problems, page performance, mobile rendering, and structured data.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Lesson 08 is eight hours of technical SEO and the capstone audit depends on it, but D1-S1-C02 is scoped to on-page and off-page tactics and D1-S1-C03 to ranking factors; neither covers diagnosis and remediation of technical defects.
